subject: DPA negotiation: Finovate Systems — round 1 edits & counsel questions
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@finovate.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 10 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed DPA edits (round 1) — Finovate Systems

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Attached is our first-pass redline of the standard Redwood DPA with a short summary tab that highlights the three items we expect will be the main negotiation points: subprocessors, audit scope / audit frequency, and international data transfers.

Quick notes:
- Subprocessors: we kept our standard subprocessor carve (we list CloudArc, ClearSight analytics, and LogFlow) and propose a 30-day notice for additions.
- Transfers: we included SCCs + our standard technical/organizational controls; if you need EU data residency guarantees we can discuss options in Dedicated.
- Audit: we limited audits to annually with a scoped checklist; if Finovate needs more frequent attestation we can propose a SOC2 addendum priced separately.

I copied Mina (privacy counsel) and Lauren (your GS contact) — Mina, could you do a quick pass on the attached and flag anything we should expect the customer counsel to push back on?

Attachments: Finovate_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (redline), redline_summary.xlsx (summary)

Next steps: Sarah — if the redline looks reasonable, happy to take another call this week to walk through the three hot spots and agree on language to send to your legal.

Best,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
-priyom_das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Sarah Lin <sarah@finovate.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: dpa-legal@finovate.com, tom@classiccounsel.com
Date: Sun, 11 May 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA edits (round 1) — Finovate Systems

Thanks, Priyom — received and forwarded to our external counsel for review (Tom) and our in-house privacy team. A couple of quick clarifying questions from us before Tom dives in:

1) Subprocessor transparency: your 30-day notice is fine but our policy requires a prior right to object for subprocessors that will process payment card data or customer analytics. Can you confirm whether ClearSight ever processes PII linked to payment transactions?

2) Data transfers: you reference SCCs — do you have an executed DTA for US <-> EU transfers, or will SCCs be executed per customer? We need certainty for regulatory reviews.

3) Audit access: our legal is requesting audit rights for two years and the ability to perform a security questionnaire more than once per year in case of material incidents. Are those negotiable?

Tom will send a marked-up set after he reviews; head's up that Finovate's legal usually pushes for stronger notice periods on subprocessor additions and a broader definition of personal data.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sarah
Director of Integrations | Finovate Systems
-sarah@finovate.com

----

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposed DPA edits (round 1) — comments for negotiation prep

Priyom / Lauren — my read after quick pass and cross-check with playbook:

- Subprocessors: expect pushback on 30 days. Acceptable compromise is to offer 30 days notice plus prior written notice + objection right limited to objectively demonstrable security/compliance risk. Do not agree to blanket prior consent for all subprocessors.
- ClearSight: per our contracts they do not process cardholder data (payments are tokenized via PaymentHub). We should confirm with Ops, but we can state "no payment card data processed" in the response and offer a SOC2 report.
- Transfers: SCCs executed per customer is standard for us; we can mention that we also support enterprise specific DTAs for committed Dedicated deployments. Avoid wording that suggests we maintain a global DTA.
- Audit frequency: keep to annual audits; offer an incident-triggered one-off assessment (paid) if there is a material incident. Two-year audit retention is okay to confirm as part of attestation docs, but avoid unlimited or unrestricted live audits.

Suggested language snippets I can insert into the response to Finovate legal. I attached a PDF with margin notes.

Attachment: finovate_privacy_counsel_comments.pdf

Mina Haddad
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
-mina_haddad@redwood.ai

----

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@finovate.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA edits (round 1) — Finovate Systems

Sarah —
Thanks for the fast turn. We incorporated Mina's suggested language and prepared a short cover note for your counsel to try to accelerate. Two items to call out in the cover note:

1) Subprocessors: we offer 30-day notice + limited objection right (only for objectively demonstrable security/compliance risk). We explicitly confirm ClearSight does not receive payment cardholder data; we can provide their SOC2 upon request.
2) Transfers: SCCs are executed per customer; we can offer a DTA for Dedicated deployments where residency is contractually required.
3) Audit: annual attestation; incident-triggered assessments available (cost-recoverable).

I attached the updated redline (v1.1) and a short summary spreadsheet. If Tom wants to send back specific redlines, Mina can patch language directly. Also, if these terms look acceptable I can prepare the DocuSign envelope with the updated DPA (we use DocuSign) and send for signature — timeline estimate: 1–2 business days to issue.

Attachments: Finovate_DPA_Redline_v1.1.docx (redline), redline_summary.xlsx

Best,
Priyom

From: Tom Reeves <tom@classiccounsel.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lin <sarah@finovate.com>
Cc: dpa-legal@finovate.com
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Finovate redline (round 1) — comments attached

Priyom / team — attached is Finovate's marked-up DPA. High-level:
- Subprocessors: we redlined a shorter notice period (15 days) and a prior objection right for subprocessors that will "process or materially impact Personal Data"; that is broader than your proposed carve.
- Transfers: asked for explicit confirmation that SCCs will be executed per agreement and a clause requiring notice if Redwood intends to transfer to a country without an adequacy decision.
- Audit: requested the ability to perform a security questionnaire up to twice a year and audit rights for two years after termination.

We are willing to be pragmatic on notice periods if Redwood agrees to stronger transparency (monthly subprocessor list and quicker notice for high-risk additions).

Attachment(s): Finovate_DPA_Redline_Finovate_v1.pdf

On a separate practical point: Sarah, when we get close please send the final text and I will coordinate a DocuSign envelope. We prefer DocuSign and will need the signature block for both parties and a simple SOW reference.

Regards,
Tom Reeves
Classic Counsel (external counsel for Finovate)
-tom@classiccounsel.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA — next steps once we receive Finovate's final redlines

Team —
Good capture. Two quick operational asks before we respond to Tom:

1) Ops confirm on ClearSight: please get a one-line confirmation that they do not process cardholder data and whether they encrypt at rest. We need that to include in our response.
2) Sales/pricing: if Finovate insists on twice-yearly questionnaires or expanded audit scope, we should surface potential incremental cost. Lauren, please prepare a short pricing note for the CS/AM covering incident-assessment fees and additional attestation costs.

Once we have Ops and pricing, I authorize Priyom to send a redline response back to Tom with our counter-proposals and a DocuSign-ready copy. Aim to close before end of next week.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Revenue | Redwood Inference
